problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,0,-3)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=⟨-3,2,0⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨0,0,1⟩.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Cartesian Equation of a Plane

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨2,-4,3⟩.$

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 4 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =11i+1j+4k \\  & =⟨11,1,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨11,1,4⟩ & =⟨2,-4,3⟩\cdot ⟨11,1,4⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨11,1,4⟩ & =30\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨11,1,4⟩ & =30 \\ 11x+y+4z & =30 \\ 11x+y+4z-30 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
